Multi-pathway reprogramming of endothelial plasticity in diabetic heart and aorta

Multi-pathway reprogramming of endothelial plasticity in diabetic heart and aorta. (A) Progressive EC state trajectory. Early diabetes shows expansion of angiogenic and EC-1 progenitor-like clusters with impaired proliferative capacity, alongside transiently adaptive lipid-handling populations. ECs progressively transition from angiogenic-homeostatic states with depletion of shear-responsive clusters toward inflammatory-injury clusters, with late-stage emergence of EndoMT-like, Impdh1 + pyroptotic, and metabolically exhausted populations, reflecting progressive loss of regenerative potential. (B) Cell-intrinsic signaling pathways. In health, active YAP drives KDR (VEGFR2) expression enabling VEGF-KDR signaling, while HIF-1α/HIF-2α heterodimerize with ARNT under hypoxia to induce VEGF transcription. Diabetic stress impairs angiogenesis through decreased YAP activity reducing KDR expression, ARNT downregulation reducing HIF-1α/ARNT dimerization and weakening hypoxic VEGF induction, and progressive Ets1 and Stat5 loss. EndoMT and fibrotic programming are driven by SOX4 upregulation inducing mesenchymal markers while suppressing endothelial identity genes, indirectly reversible by metformin; and ATF3 directly activating TGF-β2 transcription and promoting apoptosis specifically in late-stage venous ECs. KLF11 upregulation epigenetically represses TXNIP, SNAI1, and NOTCH1 promoters via to counteract EndoMT, but proves insufficiently protective. Igfbp5 upregulation in late-stage EC clusters promotes fibrosis; Impdh1 marks the terminal differentiation trajectory driving pyroptosis; Irf7 enrichment amplifies interferon-stimulated gene expression promoting inflammation; and heat shock protein suppression impairs proteostatic buffering capacity under metabolic stress. (C) Multicellular crosstalk. Pericyte TNFα suppresses angiogenic endothelial subclusters while activating inflammatory transcription and SASP factors; targeted by adalimumab, infliximab, etanercept, and MAR001. Macrophage IL-1β engages endothelial IL1R1/IL1RAP progressively amplifying Cxcl1 and Vcam1 expression promoting leukocyte adhesion and endothelial injury; targeted by anakinra, canakinumab, nadunolimab, and AMG-108. Cardiomyocyte ANGPTL4 signals via endothelial CDH5/SDC3 promoting pathological angiogenesis; targeted by MAR001. Fisetin targets endothelial senescence. EndoMT-like ECs release fibronectin promoting VSMC activation and ECM deposition; VSMCs reciprocally release IGFBP2, predicted to reinforce EC dysfunction, though experimental validation remains pending. EC PDGFB/PDGFD activates PDGFR + fibroblasts driving fibroblast expansion and cardiac fibrosis, with fibroblasts reciprocally secreting PDGFB perpetuating vascular stress; targeted by imatinib and anti-PDGF-BB DARPins. Tgfbr2 enrichment in EndMT + ECs provides rationale for TGFβRI/II targeting by galunisertib to suppress EndoMT-driven fibrotic remodeling. Red therapeutics; repurposing/blue; preclinical. Abbreviations listed in Supplementary Table S1. Generated using BioRender
